title: Tenali Raman: The Triumph of the Vikatakavi
summary: On the twentieth anniversary of King Krishnadevaraya’s coronation, an imperial assembly of poets, scholars, and monarchs from across Bharatavarsha gathered in the Grand Hall of ...
full_text:
On the twentieth anniversary of King Krishnadevaraya’s coronation, an imperial assembly of poets, scholars, and monarchs from across Bharatavarsha gathered in the Grand Hall of Victory at Vijayanagara.
The royal court poet laureate, Allasani Peddana, stood before the assembly and presented a gold-embroidered crown of pearls to the Emperor, praising his reign as the Golden Age of Literature and Justice.

King Krishnadevaraya took the pearl crown in his hands.
He did not place it upon his own head.
The Emperor stood up from his Golden Throne, walked down the marble steps into the center of the hall, and approached Tenali Raman!

The court watched in breathless silence.
King Krishnadevaraya placed the pearl crown upon Tenali Raman’s head, and proclaimed before the entire empire:
'Scholars and kings of Bharatavarsha!
Many emperors have armies, fortresses, and treasuries of diamonds.
But the greatest treasure of Vijayanagara has been our *Vikatakavi*—Tenali Raman!

When flattery blinded my eyes, his wit gave me sight.
When anger inflamed my sword, his humor poured cooling water upon my heart.
When corruption oppressed the poor, his courage held up the mirror of justice before power.
He never flattered a monarch for gold, nor did he ever despise a humble beggar.
His laughter was the shield of the innocent, his poetry was the music of truth, and his wisdom preserved the soul of our empire!'

Tenali Raman bowed low, tears of profound emotion in his eyes.
He took off the pearl crown and placed it gently at the Emperor’s feet:
'Maharaj, a crown belongs on the head of a righteous king who loves his people.
My only crown is the joy of our citizens, the laughter in your halls, and the truth that unites our hearts.'

The entire assembly of ten thousand dignitaries, soldiers, and citizens erupted in thunderous, standing applause that echoed across the Tungabhadra River and down the corridors of history.
And so the legend of Tenali Raman lived on for centuries—remembered not merely as a jester who made a king laugh, but as the eternal poet of wisdom, courage, and righteous wit who proved that a single honest laugh can illuminate the darkest world.
moral: The true jester does not merely provoke laughter; he wields wit as the shield of justice, the sword of truth, and the soul of wisdom.
